verdicts.why: Carl Lucas joined the Marines (Diamondback, LC S1 ep 11) and then became a Savannah cop (Reva calls him a former cop in an ep 4 flashback) before Seagate. Both are past groups, so they go first, keyed to his first title (Jessica Jones S1), Marines before police. The record had him leaving Harlem's Paradise for them.

The screen names her child-star show It's Patsy (theme song, JJ S1 eps 3-5) and shows it in JJ S1 ep 11. It is a past employer like Trish Talk, keyed to her first title and placed first. It runs through all three seasons, so it is not a minor job.

held: minor employer. Malcolm takes Pryce Cheng's offer only in JJ S2 ep 13, the same scene that brings him to Hogarth & Associates (his real next stage). It is a single minor job seen once, so it stays an open owner question.

Dorothy founded and runs her talent agency, Stars & Tykes Talent Agency. She is seen at work there in JJ S1 ep 7 (with the agency slogan) and in S2 ep 2, and it is mentioned in S3 eps 9-10. A company counts. She is never shown leaving it, and her death is not a departure.

In Guardians of the Galaxy (a title his record already uses) Thanos commands his daughters Gamora and Nebula and lends them to Ronan. Their records, and the owner's rule, put them in the Children of Thanos from this film, so his stage for the group starts there, not at Infinity War.

In Item 47 they are bank robbers until Sitwell offers them S.H.I.E.L.D. jobs at the end (Benny in R&D, Claire as Agent Blake's assistant). So they join during their first title; the dataset keys such joins to the title (e.g. Rogue, X-Men), not "(from the start)".

Savin is a former U.S. Army lieutenant colonel. Killian brought him into Extremis from among the war veterans (IM3: Killian 'expanded the program to include injured war veterans'). The Army is past and goes first. The A.I.M.-to-Army-to-A.I.M. loop never happens.
Brandt is a U.S. Army veteran and amputee recruited into A.I.M.'s Extremis program. The Army is past and comes before A.I.M. Nothing on screen has her return to the Army.

Thunderbolts* tells that she founded and led O.X.E. Group. When she became CIA director she publicly stepped back, but kept control in secret. All through Thunderbolts* she is still CIA director facing impeachment. So O.X.E. is past, keyed to her first title (The Falcon and the Winter Soldier), and the CIA follows it.

Marvel Database files him as Stephen Strange (Earth-TRN954) ('| Reality = Earth-TRN954'). HANDOFF also names Sinister Strange as Earth-TRN954, the same temporary-number treatment as Defender Strange (TRN953) and Binary/Beast (TRN1225). Corrected value: Earth-TRN954.

In She-Hulk ep 8 (Ribbit and Rip It), Eugene leads a crew of hired men at the Lily Pad and names them on screen ('Guys, what do we think about the name Leap Squad?'). A crew counts, and its leader is in it. The name is said on screen; some of his men suggest 'Tadpoles' instead.

Daredevil S3 tells Dex's past in order: the Army after Eileen Mercer's death, then the suicide hotline, then the FBI (Quantico). In ep 6 the FBI makes him step down and give up his badge, and Fisk then recruits him. He turns on Fisk in ep 13. Same groups, in the right order: Army, FBI, Fisk's Empire.

Vanessa works at Scene Contempo Gallery in Daredevil S1. Fisk meets and buys from her there (eps 3-4), Matt visits her there (ep 9), and Karen says the name on screen ('It says she works at Scene Contempo Gallery'). It is a real workplace seen more than once, keyed to her first title.

Nobu sits in Fisk's alliance as the Hand's representative ('those I speak for', S1 ep 5). His Hand men and ninja garb are shown in S1 (eps 1, 7, 9), and S2 tells that he was the Hand all along and the Yakuza was a front. Under the past-group rule, the Hand goes at the front in S1. The S2 stage stays.

Vladimir and Anatoly built their own Russian operation in New York after escaping Utkin Prison (ep 4 flashback). Wesley then brings them into Fisk's alliance. After Fisk kills Anatoly (ep 5), Vladimir turns on him. So: Mafia, then Fisk's Empire, then the Mafia again; his last stage is unchanged.

Blake is an NYPD detective at the 15th Precinct who, with Hoffman, goes on Fisk's payroll, and he is still a cop when Hoffman kills him. The NYPD comes first, then Fisk's Empire. The Fisk-to-NYPD-to-Fisk loop never happens.

Marvel Database gives her '| Reality = Unknown'. Its Earth-TRN872 is not a world but a catch-all for people the TVA sent to the Void with no known home ('Rather than being a distinct reality...'). The dataset already keeps the other Void people (Dogpool, Nicepool, Ladypool) at null for this reason, and HANDOFF places her in The Void. Corrected value: null (unchanged).
